title: Telegram Symbols: Copy & Paste for Names, Bios & Channels
meta_description: Copy and paste Telegram symbols for your name, bio and channel posts: paper-plane arrows, name frames like ꧁ ꧂, trend letters, dividers and ready-made combos.
hero_tagline: Paper-plane arrows, name frames, trend letters and dividers for your Telegram name, bio and channel posts. Click any symbol to copy it.
intro: Telegram symbols go in the places that show your personality: your display name, your bio, group titles and channel posts. This page groups them by job. Arrowheads that echo Telegram's paper-plane logo, frames like ꧁ ꧂ that wrap a name, the rare letters behind the "symbol on Telegram" name trend, and dividers and bullets that make a long channel post easy to scan.

sections.label: Logo Lookalikes
sections.intro: Unicode has no Telegram logo, so channel names borrow its paper-plane shape from arrowheads and aircraft.

sections.label: Name Frames
sections.h2: Frames and Wings for Your Telegram Name
sections.intro: Paste one on each side of your first name, like ꧁ Alex ꧂ or 『 Alex 』. Always paste them as a pair so the name looks balanced.

sections.label: Trend Letters
sections.h2: Rare Letters From the "Symbol on Telegram" Trend
sections.intro: Letters from Batak, Vai, Buginese and other scripts that the name trend uses as decoration. Each name notes the script it comes from.

sections.label: Stars & Hearts
sections.intro: Small accents for a bio or a display name. One or two is plenty in a 70-character bio.

sections.label: Post Markers
sections.h2: Bullets and Markers for Channel Posts
sections.intro: Channel posts are long and read on a phone. Start each line with a marker and readers can skim the list.

sections.label: Dividers
sections.h2: Dividers for Channel Posts and Group Descriptions
sections.intro: Each button copies the whole line. Use them between sections of a post, not in a bio, where they eat most of the character limit.

sections.label: Combos
sections.h2: Ready-Made Telegram Name and Channel Combos
sections.intro: Copy a finished decoration in one click. The Javanese wing frame leaves a gap in the middle for your name.

editorial_sections.label: Where They Work
editorial_sections.h2: Where Telegram Accepts Symbols, and Where It Doesn't
paragraphs: Your first and last name, your bio, group titles and channel names all take any Unicode character, so everything on this page pastes straight in. Your @username does not. Telegram only allows the letters a to z, the digits 0 to 9 and underscores there, so put the decoration in your display name instead. That is the name people see in chats anyway.

The bio is where space runs out. Telegram caps it at 70 characters, or 140 with Premium, and every symbol counts against that. A long divider can use a sixth of it, so keep bio decoration to one or two characters and save dividers for channel posts.

Premium custom emoji are a different thing. They are images from Telegram's own emoji packs, not Unicode characters, so they only display inside Telegram. Copy a message that contains them into another app and each one turns into the ordinary emoji it was built on. To style the letters themselves, use the Telegram font generator.

editorial_sections.label: The Name Trend
paragraphs: Much of the search for Telegram symbols comes from a TikTok trend: rewriting your name so each letter becomes a rare character from another script, such as ᯓ from Batak or ꕤ from Vai. To convert a whole name at once, use the Name to Symbols converter. The frames and combos above are for dressing up the result.

Rare scripts carry one risk. A phone without a font for Batak or Vai shows an empty box instead of the letter. Before you set a new name, send it to your own Saved Messages and open it on a second device. The frames, stars and dividers on this page come from blocks that almost every phone can display.

sources: Telegram's client configuration reference sets the bio limit at 70 characters for regular accounts and 140 for Premium accounts. Telegram's FAQ states that a username can use a-z, 0-9 and underscores.

faq.q: Can I put symbols in my Telegram username?
faq.a: No. A Telegram @username only accepts the letters a to z, the digits 0 to 9 and underscores. Put symbols in your first or last name instead, which is what other people see in chats.

faq.q: Is there a Telegram logo symbol I can copy?
faq.a: No, Unicode has no character for Telegram's paper-plane logo. The closest lookalikes are the arrowheads ➢ and ➤, the conical taper ⌲ and the airplane ✈.

faq.q: Why does my Telegram name show empty boxes on a friend's phone?
faq.a: Their phone has no font for that character, which happens most with rare scripts like Batak and Vai. Send the name to your Saved Messages and check it on another device before you set it.

faq.q: How many symbols fit in a Telegram bio?
faq.a: A Telegram bio holds 70 characters, or 140 with Premium, and every symbol counts toward that total. Keep bio decoration to one or two symbols and leave the rest for text.
